Special functions

Source: vignettes/special-functions.Rmd
special-functions.Rmd

symcompR includes the elementary and special functions of SymPy. Each one evaluates exactly at special points, stays symbolic elsewhere, knows its derivative and series expansion, can be rewritten in terms of related functions, and evaluates numerically with N().

library(symcompR)
x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y"); z <- Symbol("z")
a <- Symbol("a"); b <- Symbol("b"); nu <- Symbol("nu")
n <- Symbol("n", integer = TRUE)
xp <- Symbol("xp", positive = TRUE)
f <- Function("f")

A note on arguments: when a function also exists in base R (such as exp() or gamma()), a plain R number gives a plain R number. Wrap numbers in S(), Integer(), or Rational() to get exact results.

gamma(5)
#> [1] 24
gamma(S(5))
#> 24
sym_atan2(S(1), S(1))
#> pi/4

Elementary functions 

acos(Rational(1, 2))
#> pi/3
asin(S(1))
#> pi/2
atan(oo)
#> pi/2
acosh(S(1))
#> 0
sinc(0)
#> 1
log(S(8), 2)
#> 3
exp(log(x))
#> x
log(exp(x))
#> log(exp(x))
log(exp(xp))
#> xp
root(8, 3)
#> 2
cbrt(-8)
#> 2*(-1)^(1/3)
real_root(-8, 3)
#> -2

log(exp(x)) is not simplified for a general symbol, because the identity fails for complex x; it holds for the positive symbol xp. Note also that cbrt(-8) is the principal cube root, while real_root() gives the real one.

Rewriting changes the form of an expression:

rewrite(sinh(x), "exp")
#> exp(x)/2 - exp(-x)/2
rewrite(cos(x), "exp")
#> exp(I*x)/2 + exp(-I*x)/2
rewrite(tan(x), "sin")
#> 2*sin(x)^2/sin(2*x)

Complex parts and rounding 

Abs(-3 + 4 * sym_I)
#> 5
re(exp(sym_I * x))
#> exp(-im(x))*cos(re(x))
arg(1 + sym_I)
#> pi/4
conjugate(2 + 3 * sym_I)
#> 2 - 3*I
sign(S(-3))
#> -1
floor(Rational(7, 2))
#> 3
ceiling(-Rational(7, 2))
#> -3
frac(Rational(7, 2))
#> 1/2
Max(1, x, 3, x)
#> Max(3, x)
Min(xp, -1)
#> -1

Gamma and related functions 

gamma(Rational(1, 2))
#> sqrt(pi)
gamma(Rational(-3, 2))
#> 4*sqrt(pi)/3
diff(gamma(x), x)
#> gamma(x)*polygamma(0, x)
rewrite(gamma(x + 1), "factorial")
#> factorial(x)
loggamma(S(3))
#> log(2)
polygamma(0, 1)
#> -EulerGamma
polygamma(1, 1)
#> pi^2/6
diff(digamma_sym(x), x)
#> polygamma(1, x)
sym_beta(S(2), S(3))
#> 1/12
rewrite(sym_beta(x, y), "gamma")
#> gamma(x)*gamma(y)/gamma(x + y)
lowergamma(1, x)
#> 1 - exp(-x)
uppergamma(1, x)
#> exp(-x)
uppergamma(Rational(1, 2), x)
#> sqrt(pi)*erfc(sqrt(x))

Factorials and binomial coefficients:

sym_factorial(S(5))
#> 120
factorial2(7)
#> 105
RisingFactorial(x, 3)
#> x*(x + 1)*(x + 2)
FallingFactorial(x, 3)
#> x*(x - 2)*(x - 1)
sym_binomial(10, 3)
#> 120

Zeta and polylogarithm 

zeta(2)
#> pi^2/6
zeta(4)
#> pi^4/90
zeta(-1)
#> -1/12
zeta(0)
#> -1/2
zeta(3)
#> zeta(3)
dirichlet_eta(1)
#> log(2)
polylog(2, Rational(1, 2))
#> -log(2)^2/2 + pi^2/12
expand_func(polylog(1, x))
#> -log(1 - x)
lerchphi(1, 2, 1)
#> lerchphi(1, 2, 1)

zeta(3) (Apéry’s constant) has no known closed form, so it stays unevaluated.

Error functions and integrals

erf2(x, y) is the two argument error function \mathrm{erf}(y) - \mathrm{erf}(x).

erf(0)
#> 0
erf(oo)
#> 1
erf(-x)
#> -erf(x)
diff(erf(x), x)
#> 2*exp(-x^2)/sqrt(pi)
rewrite(erfc(x), "erf")
#> 1 - erf(x)
erfinv(0)
#> 0
erf2(0, x)
#> erf(x)
series(erf(x), x, 0, 6)
#> 2*x/sqrt(pi) - 2*x^3/(3*sqrt(pi)) + x^5/(5*sqrt(pi)) + O(x^6)

The exponential, logarithmic, sine, cosine, and Fresnel integrals. Li() is the offset logarithmic integral, \mathrm{li}(x) - \mathrm{li}(2), which vanishes at 2:

diff(Ei(x), x)
#> exp(x)/x
diff(li(x), x)
#> 1/log(x)
Li(2)
#> 0
diff(Si(x), x)
#> sin(x)/x
diff(Ci(x), x)
#> cos(x)/x
Si(oo)
#> pi/2
rewrite(expint(1, x), "Ei")
#> -Ei(x*exp_polar(I*pi)) + I*pi
E1(x)
#> expint(1, x)
fresnels(oo)
#> 1/2
diff(fresnels(x), x)
#> sin(pi*x^2/2)

Bessel and Airy functions 

diff(besselj(nu, x), x)
#> besselj(nu - 1, x)/2 - besselj(nu + 1, x)/2
besselj(0, 0)
#> 1
besseli(0, 0)
#> 1
besselj(-2, x)
#> besselj(2, x)
diff(bessely(0, x), x)
#> -bessely(1, x)
diff(besselk(nu, x), x)
#> -besselk(nu - 1, x)/2 - besselk(nu + 1, x)/2
rewrite(hankel1(nu, x), "besselj")
#> hankel1(nu, x)

Bessel functions of half integer order and the spherical Bessel functions are elementary:

expand_func(besselj(Rational(1, 2), x))
#> besselj(1/2, x)
expand_func(jn(0, x))
#> sin(x)/x
expand_func(jn(1, x))
#> -cos(x)/x + sin(x)/x^2

The Airy function \mathrm{Ai} solves y'' = x y:

airyai(0)
#> 3^(1/3)/(3*gamma(2/3))
diff(airyai(x), x, 2)
#> x*airyai(x)

Elliptic integrals 

elliptic_k(0)
#> pi/2
elliptic_e(0)
#> pi/2
diff(elliptic_k(x), x)
#> (-(1 - x)*elliptic_k(x) + elliptic_e(x))/(2*x*(1 - x))
series(elliptic_k(x), x, 0, 3)
#> pi/2 + pi*x/8 + 9*pi*x^2/128 + O(x^3)

Hypergeometric functions

hyper(ap, bq, z) is the generalized hypergeometric function {}_pF_q, and meijerg() is the Meijer G function. hyperexpand() rewrites them in terms of named functions when possible.

hyper(list(1, 1), list(2), z)
#> hyper((1, 1), (2,), z)
hyperexpand(hyper(list(1, 1), list(2), z))
#> -log(1 - z)/z
hyperexpand(hyper(list(), list(), z))
#> exp(z)
hyperexpand(hyper(list(Rational(1, 2)), list(Rational(3, 2)), -z^2))
#> sqrt(pi)*erf(z)/(2*z)
G <- meijerg(list(list(1, 1), list()), list(list(1), list(0)), z)
G
#> meijerg(((1, 1), ()), ((1,), (0,)), z)
hyperexpand(G)
#> log(z + 1)

Orthogonal polynomials 

legendre(3, x)
#> 5*x^3/2 - 3*x/2
assoc_legendre(2, 1, x)
#> -3*x*sqrt(1 - x^2)
chebyshevt(4, x)
#> 8*x^4 - 8*x^2 + 1
chebyshevu(3, x)
#> 8*x^3 - 4*x
hermite(3, x)
#> 8*x^3 - 12*x
laguerre(3, x)
#> -x^3/6 + 3*x^2/2 - 3*x + 1
diff(legendre(n, x), x)
#> n*(x*legendre(n, x) - legendre(n - 1, x))/(x^2 - 1)

Orthogonality of the Legendre polynomials on [-1, 1]:

sym_integrate(legendre(2, x) * legendre(3, x), list(x, -1, 1))
#> 0

Spherical harmonics:

expand_func(Ynm(1, 0, x, y))
#> sqrt(3)*cos(x)/(2*sqrt(pi))

Lambert W, Heaviside, and Dirac delta 

LambertW(0)
#> 0
LambertW(-1 / sym_E)
#> -1
LambertW(sym_E)
#> 1
diff(LambertW(x), x)
#> LambertW(x)/(x*(LambertW(x) + 1))
Heaviside(0)
#> 1/2
diff(Heaviside(x), x)
#> DiracDelta(x)
sym_integrate(DiracDelta(x) * cos(x), list(x, -oo, oo))
#> 1
sym_integrate(DiracDelta(x - 2) * x^2, list(x, 0, 5))
#> 4
KroneckerDelta(1, 2)
#> 0

SingularityFunction(x, a, n) is the Macaulay bracket \langle x - a \rangle^n used in beam deflection problems.

diff(SingularityFunction(x, 3, 2), x)
#> 2*SingularityFunction(x, 3, 1)

Piecewise functions

Piecewise() takes pairs list(expression, condition); the first condition that holds selects the value, and TRUE acts as “otherwise”.

p <- Piecewise(list(x^2, Lt(x, 0)), list(x, TRUE))
p
#> Piecewise((x^2, x < 0), (x, True))
subs(p, x, -2)
#> 4
diff(p, x)
#> Piecewise((2*x, x < 0), (1, True))
sym_integrate(p, list(x, -1, 1))
#> 5/6
piecewise_fold(Piecewise(list(1, Lt(x, 0)), list(2, TRUE)) + 1)
#> Piecewise((2, x < 0), (3, True))
rewrite(Heaviside(x), "Piecewise")
#> Piecewise((0, x < 0), (1/2, Eq(x, 0)), (1, True))

bspline_basis(d, knots, i, x) is the i-th B-spline of degree d (counting from zero), as a piecewise polynomial.

bspline_basis(1, list(0, 1, 2), 0, x)
#> Piecewise((x, (x >= 0) & (x <= 1)), (2 - x, (x >= 1) & (x <= 2)), (0, True))
bspline_basis(2, list(0, 1, 2, 3), 0, x)
#> Piecewise((x^2/2, (x >= 0) & (x <= 1)), (-x^2 + 3*x - 3/2, (x >= 1) & (x <= 2)), (x^2/2 - 3*x + 9/2, (x >= 2) & (x <= 3)), (0, True))
bspline_basis_set(2, list(0, 1, 2, 3), x)[[1]]
#> Piecewise((x^2/2, (x >= 0) & (x <= 1)), (-x^2 + 3*x - 3/2, (x >= 1) & (x <= 2)), (x^2/2 - 3*x + 9/2, (x >= 2) & (x <= 3)), (0, True))
interpolating_spline(1, x, list(1, 2, 4), list(3, 4, 7))
#> Piecewise((x + 2, (x >= 1) & (x <= 2)), (3*x/2 + 1, (x >= 2) & (x <= 4)))

Numerical evaluation

N(expr, n) evaluates to n significant digits.

N(gamma(Rational(1, 3)), 30)
#> 2.67893853470774763365569294097
N(zeta(3), 30)
#> 1.20205690315959428539973816151
N(erf(1), 25)
#> 0.8427007929497148693412206
N(elliptic_k(Rational(1, 2)), 20)
#> 1.8540746773013719184
N(EulerGamma, 30)
#> 0.577215664901532860606512090082
N(Catalan, 30)
#> 0.915965594177219015054603514932
N(legendre(5, Rational(3, 10)), 20)
#> 0.34538625000000000000

Some functions evaluate in double precision only, so they are limited to 15 significant digits:

N(besselj(0, 1))
#> 0.765197686557967
N(airyai(1))
#> 0.135292416312881
N(LambertW(1))
#> 0.567143290409784
N(Si(1))
#> 0.946083070367183
N(li(10))
#> 6.16559950478730
N(hyper(list(1, 2), list(3), Rational(1, 2)))
#> 1.54517744447956

More elementary functions

The reciprocal trigonometric and hyperbolic functions and their inverses:

a <- Symbol("a"); b <- Symbol("b")
csc(sym_pi / 6)
#> 2
acsc(2)
#> pi/6
asec(2)
#> pi/3
acot(1)
#> pi/4
diff(acot(x), x)
#> -1/(x^2 + 1)
sech(0)
#> 1
asech(1)
#> 0
rewrite(coth(x), "exp")
#> (exp(x) + exp(-x))/(exp(x) - exp(-x))
rewrite(coth(x), "tanh")
#> 1/tanh(x)
rewrite(acoth(2), "log")
#> log(3/2)/2 + log(2)/2
rewrite(acsch(1), "log")
#> log(1 + sqrt(2))
diff(csch(x), x)
#> -coth(x)*csch(x)
im(3 + 4 * sym_I)
#> 4

More special functions

Further Bessel, Airy, and related functions. yn(), hn1(), and hn2() are spherical Bessel and Hankel functions, and jn_zeros() finds zeros of the spherical Bessel functions numerically.

rewrite(yn(0, x), "sin")
#> yn(0, x)
expand_func(yn(1, x))
#> -sin(x)/x - cos(x)/x^2
rewrite(hankel2(0, x), "besselj")
#> hankel2(0, x)
rewrite(hn1(0, x), "sin")
#> hn1(0, x)
expand_func(hn2(0, x))
#> sin(x)/x + I*cos(x)/x
lapply(jn_zeros(0, 2), N)
#> [[1]]
#> 3.14159265358979
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> 6.28318530717959
N(airybi(0))
#> 0.614926627446001
N(airyaiprime(0))
#> -0.258819403792807
airybiprime(0)
#> 3^(1/6)/gamma(1/3)
diff(airybi(x), x)
#> airybiprime(x)

Integrals and inverses: hyperbolic sine and cosine integrals, the Fresnel cosine integral, the imaginary error function, and inverse error functions.

N(Chi(1))
#> 0.837866940980208
N(Shi(1))
#> 1.05725087537573
diff(Shi(x), x)
#> sinh(x)/x
N(fresnelc(1))
#> 0.779893400376823
limit(fresnelc(x), x, oo)
#> 1/2
rewrite(erfi(x), "erf")
#> -I*erf(I*x)
N(erfi(1))
#> 1.65042575879754
erfcinv(1)
#> 0
N(erfcinv(Rational(1, 2)))
#> 0.476936276204470
erf2inv(0, y)
#> erfinv(y)

Elliptic integrals of the first and third kind:

N(elliptic_f(Rational(1, 2), Rational(1, 3)))
#> 0.506847756265431
elliptic_f(0, x)
#> 0
N(elliptic_pi(Rational(1, 3), Rational(1, 2)))
#> 2.31079499075428

Orthogonal polynomials with numeric parameters, and integer sequences:

assoc_laguerre(2, 1, x)
#> x^2/2 - 3*x + 3
gegenbauer(3, 2, x)
#> 32*x^3 - 12*x
jacobi(2, 1, 1, x)
#> 15*x^2/4 - 3/4
jacobi_normalized(2, 1, 1, x)
#> sqrt(42)*(15*x^2/4 - 3/4)/6
hermite_prob(3, x)
#> x^3 - 3*x
genocchi(6)
#> -3
lapply(0:7, tribonacci)
#> [[1]]
#> 0
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> 1
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> 1
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> 2
#> 
#> [[5]]
#> 4
#> 
#> [[6]]
#> 7
#> 
#> [[7]]
#> 13
#> 
#> [[8]]
#> 24
lapply(0:7, andre)
#> [[1]]
#> 1
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> 1
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> 1
#> 
#> [[4]]
#> 2
#> 
#> [[5]]
#> 5
#> 
#> [[6]]
#> 16
#> 
#> [[7]]
#> 61
#> 
#> [[8]]
#> 272

More functions from sympy.functions.special: the Riemann \xi function, Stieltjes constants, the multivariate gamma function, Owen’s T function, the Marcum Q function, Jacobi theta functions, the Appell F_1 function, and the incomplete beta functions.

riemann_xi(2)
#> pi/6
stieltjes(0)
#> EulerGamma
multigamma(3, 2)
#> 3*pi/2
owens_t(0, a)
#> atan(a)/(2*pi)
N(owens_t(1, Rational(1, 2)))
#> 0.0430646911207854
marcumq(1, 0, b)
#> exp(-b^2/2)
N(jtheta(3, 1, Rational(1, 2)))
#> 0.505893885730485
N(appellf1(1, 1, 1, 2, Rational(1, 2), Rational(1, 3)))
#> 1.72609243471069
betainc(1, 1, 0, x)
#> betainc(1, 1, 0, x)
N(betainc_regularized(2, 3, 0, Rational(1, 2)))
#> 0.687500000000000
Rem(7, -3)
#> 1
Rem(x^2, x)
#> Rem(x^2, x)

The Mathieu functions are available as symbolic functions:

mathieus(a, b, x)
#> mathieus(a, b, x)
mathieuc(a, b, x)
#> mathieuc(a, b, x)
mathieusprime(a, b, x)
#> mathieusprime(a, b, x)
mathieucprime(a, b, x)
#> mathieucprime(a, b, x)

Ynm_c() is the complex conjugate of the spherical harmonic and Znm() the real spherical harmonic:

expand_func(Ynm_c(1, 0, a, b))
#> sqrt(3)*cos(a)/(2*sqrt(pi))
expand_func(Znm(1, 0, a, b))
#> sqrt(3)*cos(a)/(2*sqrt(pi))

Motzkin numbers and subfactorials

motzkin(n) counts the ways to draw nonintersecting chords between n points on a circle, and subfactorial(n) counts the derangements of n objects.

sapply(0:7, function(i) sstr(motzkin(i)))
#> [1] "1"  "1"  "1"  "2"  "4"  "9"  "21" "51"
subfactorial(5)
#> 44
rewrite(subfactorial(n), "uppergamma")
#> exp(-1)*uppergamma(n + 1, -1)

Polar numbers and branches

exp_polar() is an exponential that is not reduced modulo 2\pi i, which keeps track of the branch on the Riemann surface of the logarithm. polar_lift(), principal_branch(), periodic_argument(), and unbranched_argument() work with such numbers, and unpolarify() and polarify() convert expressions.

exp_polar(0)
#> exp_polar(0)
unpolarify(exp_polar(x))
#> exp(x)
polar_lift(-1)
#> exp_polar(I*pi)
polar_lift(2 * sym_I)
#> 2*exp_polar(I*pi/2)
principal_branch(-2, 2 * sym_pi)
#> 2*exp_polar(I*pi)
periodic_argument(exp_polar(3 * sym_I * sym_pi), 2 * sym_pi)
#> pi
unbranched_argument(exp_polar(3 * sym_I * sym_pi))
#> 3*pi
polarify(exp(x) * y, subs = FALSE)
#> y*exp(x)

piecewise_exclusive() rewrites a Piecewise so that its conditions do not overlap:

piecewise_exclusive(Piecewise(list(1, x < 0), list(2, x < 1), list(3, TRUE)))
#> Piecewise((1, x < 0), (2, (x >= 0) & (x < 1)), (3, x >= 1))
